articles.title: Judge blocks X rival from using Twitter name, but allows ‘Tweet’ for now
articles.description: A federal judge temporarily barred an X rival from using the Twitter name, but found that X was likely to have abandoned the “Tweet” trademark and bird logo. The startup has since relaunched as Tweet.app.

articles.title: What will Apple’s John Ternus era look like?
articles.description: It’s officially the Ternus era at Apple. Tim Cook stepped down as CEO this week, handing the company to former hardware chief John Ternus, whose first memo promised a “huge launch next week” — timing that puts Apple’s next iPhone event on his desk before he’s even settled in. Cook isn’t going far, though: he’s staying on as Executive Chairman, focused on the kind of policy […]
articles.summary: John Ternus, previously the head of hardware at Apple, is now the CEO following Tim Cook's resignation. He is reportedly planning a significant iPhone event for the upcoming week. Tim Cook remains as Executive Chairman, focusing on policy aspects of the company.

Tim Cook remains as Executive Chairman, focusing on policy.
The leadership transition at Apple may impact its strategic direction and product release schedule.

articles.title: No little kids allowed, and other new info about Tesla’s Cybercab
articles.description: The company says no children under 13 can ride -- even with a parent. That's more restrictive than the Model Y SUVs it's using as robotaxis.
articles.summary: Tesla has announced new guidelines for its autonomous vehicle, the Cybercab, stating no children under 13 can ride, even with a parent. The company also highlighted that the Cybercab is not a true self-driving car, as a driver must be present and attentive.
points: No children under 13 can ride in the Tesla Cybercab, even with a parent present.
Tesla's Cybercab requires a driver to be present at all times.
The Cybercab has been trialed in the UK with positive feedback, though it still lacks full self-driving capabilities.
articles.insight: Tesla's Cybercab demonstrates the company's focus on autonomous technology, but also highlights that fully autonomous rides are still in development, with safety measures like a human driver requirement in place.
